    Homogeneous layers of a graded representation-finite algebra #

    Proposition 3.8(1) and Corollary 3.3 (projective-rays.tex), for an algebra graded by path length, as used for A₀ in Proposition 4.14: "Every endpoint subbimodule is homogeneous: the automorphisms that multiply a degree-d vector by a^d, for a ∈ k*, preserve its dimension, and the chain has at most one member of each dimension. Since k is infinite, invariance under those automorphisms implies homogeneity. A homogeneous lift of the one-dimensional top generates each cyclic subbimodule, and positive endpoint degrees make successive layers have strictly increasing degrees." and "In each corner, the chosen vectors represent the consecutive one-dimensional quotients of a finite chain. They therefore form a basis adapted to every member of that chain. The intersection of a two-sided ideal with the corner is one such member."

    LenGrading is a grading of the algebra by ℕ with homogeneous products; the scaling maps σ_t (scale) are multiplicative.

    source
    structure MultiplicativeBasisDeformations.LenGrading (k : Type u) [Field k] (B : Type v) [Ring B] [Algebra k B] :
    Type v

    A grading by length with homogeneous products.

    • proj : ℕ → B →ₗ[k] B
    • N : ℕ
    • proj_proj (d e : ℕ) (a : B) : (self.proj d) ((self.proj e) a) = if e = d then (self.proj e) a else 0
    • proj_ge (d : ℕ) : self.N ≤ d → self.proj d = 0
    • sum (a : B) : a = ∑ d ∈ Finset.range self.N, (self.proj d) a
    • mul_hom (d e : ℕ) (a b : B) : (self.proj (d + e)) ((self.proj d) a * (self.proj e) b) = (self.proj d) a * (self.proj e) b

            Corollary 3.3 for a homogeneous basis: its intersection with a two-sided ideal spans that ideal.
